newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RINGGIT WEAKENS TO FRESH 42-MONTH LOWS.
newsitem.headline: RINGGIT WEAKENS TO FRESH 42-MONTH LOWS.

text.p: * Ringgit falls to fresh 42-month lows on dollar demand and weakness in Singapore dollar
* Immediate upside for dollar/ringgit seen limited to 2.7950
* Trading seen volatile due to wide spreads
The ringgit weakened to a new 42-month low against the dollar in early Asian trading, but profit-taking limited further rise in the dollar, dealers said.
At 0215 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.7710/50 to a dollar, after hitting a low of 2.7930, its weakest level since February 16, 1994.

Dealers said the ringgit was pressured by persistent dollar demand from offshore players as well as weakness in the Singapore dollar which dipped to 1.50 to the U.S. dollar after an official of the country's de-facto central bank said the currency's recent exchange rate was appropriate.

"The ringgit was coming down very fast because there was no resistance as local exporters have sold almost all of their dollar positions earlier," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "Players are starting to take profits but I'm still looking at a stronger dollar."
A dealer with a European bank in Singapore said, "All the indicators are showing an overbought situation, but nobody is looking at the indicators. Everybody out there seems to be buying dollars."

Dealers said immediate upside for the dollar was likely to be capped at 2.7950 although they have not completely ruled out a rise above 2.80 for the first time since dollar/ringgit was officially floated in 1973.
Trading was expected to remain volatile due to continued wide spreads, dealers said.
